title: GPX4 binder5 → degrader: recruitment routes
objective: Convert binder5, a BindCraft-designed binder to human GPX4 (P36969), from a molecule that only binds into a degrader that lowers GPX4 protein in cells. Four mechanistically distinct recruitment routes are compared, each against a matched dead or ablated control and the binder-only reference.
coordinate_note: Coordinates are those of each assembled construct. Effector segments are labelled with the native UniProt residues they come from (STUB1 Q9UNE7, SPOP O43791); the binder is residues 2–61 of the 61-residue sequence supplied earlier, with its Met1 replaced by the construct's own start Met.

regions.name: N-terminal Met–HA–GS tag
regions.description: Start methionine, lysine-free HA epitope and a Gly-Ser spacer. It replaces the binder's own Met1, which would be an internal start codon.

regions.name: GPX4-binding domain (binder5)
regions.description: Designed 60-residue helical binder to GPX4. Affinity, epitope and intracellular engagement are not measured here.

regions.name: Flexible linker (GGGGS)2
regions.description: Shared binder–effector linker, kept constant across the library so effector identity is the main variable.

regions.name: CHIP central helical region
regions.description: Retained residues between the removed TPR repeats and the U-box; associated with CHIP homodimerisation in full-length CHIP. Its boundary within this fragment is not mapped here.

regions.name: CHIP U-box (E2-recruiting module)
regions.description: STUB1 U-box (UniProt 226–300, plus three C-terminal residues in the fragment) that recruits UbcH5-class E2s.

regions.name: SPOP BTB domain
regions.description: SPOP BTB (UniProt 173–297, with the six-residue flank before it) that mediates dimerisation and, with the 3-box, CUL3 binding.

regions.name: SPOP 3-box (CUL3-binding helices)
regions.description: Two C-terminal helices of the BTB-3-box fold (PDB 3HTM helices at 301–312 and 314–328) that contact CUL3.

regions.name: SPOP C-terminal tail
regions.description: Residues after the 3-box (UniProt 330–374), including the C-terminal nuclear localisation sequence.

regions.name: C-terminal RRRG degron
regions.description: Free-carboxylate Arg-Arg-Arg-Gly C-end degron derived from the Bonger ligand-induced degradation motif; needs the last residues of the chain.

regions.name: Degron-null C-terminal TRGN
regions.description: Matched tetrapeptide used as the no-degron control for RRRG; it keeps the length and a free C-terminus.

regions.name: CMA targeting motif (KFERQ-type, 14 residues)
regions.description: Fused KFERQ-type pentapeptides (KFERQ, QKILD, QRFFE) that recruit HSC70 for chaperone-mediated autophagy.

regions.name: Glutamine-to-alanine CTM mutant
regions.description: Rule-based inactive variant of the CMA targeting motif; positions chosen by this design, not taken from a paper.

donors.name: binder5 (sequence from the user's earlier message; assumed)
donors.note: De novo BindCraft design with no database accession. The sequence is the 61-residue string given in an earlier conversation; whether it is the intended binder5 is an assumption. The leading Met is treated as the start codon, so residues 2–61 are the 60-residue binder.

hypotheses.question: Does a folded catalytic U-box E3 module on the binder turn GPX4 engagement into GPX4 ubiquitination and loss?
hypotheses.mechanism: The binder holds GPX4 while the CHIP U-box, as a dimer, charges lysines of GPX4 with ubiquitin from UbcH5-class E2 enzymes, which sends GPX4 to the proteasome.
hypotheses.measurement: Endogenous GPX4 by immunoblot with two antibodies (or HiBiT-tagged GPX4) against the reference and the R272A construct at matched anti-HA level; unchanged GPX4 mRNA by qPCR; shortened GPX4 half-life in a cycloheximide chase; K48-linked GPX4 ubiquitination in a denaturing pulldown; rescue by bortezomib or MG132; co-immunoprecipitation of GPX4 with the binder. Keep cells in ferrostatin-1 or liproxstatin-1.
hypotheses.note: Native STUB1 already ubiquitinates GPX4, so GPX4 is a natural CHIP substrate; R272A only partly inactivates the U-box in cells.

hypotheses.question: Does recruiting a CUL3 adapter (SPOP BTB/3-box) degrade GPX4, and does that need the 3-box?
hypotheses.mechanism: The SPOP module recruits CUL3 and its RING partner and E2 next to the GPX4-binder complex, so a CRL3 complex ubiquitinates GPX4 lysines in trans.
hypotheses.measurement: GPX4 loss for SPOP against the 3-box deletion at matched anti-HA level, with rescue by MLN4924 and by bortezomib, a cycloheximide chase, GPX4 ubiquitination, and co-immunoprecipitation of CUL3 with the fusion.
hypotheses.note: Differences from the CHIP arm test route and chemistry (cullin versus U-box), not just a second E3.

hypotheses.question: Does a four-residue C-end degron suffice to degrade GPX4 through the binder?
hypotheses.mechanism: A free C-terminal RRRG recruits a cullin-RING ligase directly to the binder, which then ubiquitinates GPX4 held in the complex.
hypotheses.measurement: GPX4 loss for RRRG against TRGN at matched anti-HA level; cycloheximide chase of GPX4 and of the degrader; GPX4 ubiquitination; rescue by MLN4924 and bortezomib; dominant-negative CUL2 and CUL4 to assign the cullin.
hypotheses.note: The cullin assignment conflicts between the T-cell bioPROTAC work (CUL4) and the C-end degron surveys (CRL2).

hypotheses.question: Can a KFERQ-type motif route GPX4 to the lysosome without ubiquitination?
hypotheses.mechanism: HSC70 binds the fused motif, targets the binder-GPX4 complex to the lysosome through LAMP2A (chaperone-mediated autophagy) or to endosomes through VPS4A (microautophagy), and GPX4 is degraded there.
hypotheses.measurement: GPX4 loss for the motif construct against the Q→A control at matched anti-HA level; rescue by bafilomycin A1 or NH4Cl but not by bortezomib; LAMP2A knockdown and VPS4A dominant-negative to separate routes; co-immunoprecipitation of HSC70; cycloheximide chase.
hypotheses.note: An exploratory arm. The Q→A control uses my own choice of positions.

rationale.hypothesis: Establishes what GPX4 engagement by the binder alone does to GPX4 level, GPX4 activity and the apparent immunoblot signal, and serves as the free competitor in an excess-binder experiment.

observations.finding: DARPins without any E3 module still accelerated degradation of some targets, non-catalytically, so binder-alone loss of target is a real baseline effect.
observations.context: DARPin–target complexes in cultured cells; half-lives followed over hours.

observations.finding: The binder-only control for a CHIPΔTPR bioPROTAC acted partly through a lysosomal route.
observations.context: scFv bioPROTAC against misfolded SOD1 in cultured cells.

observations.finding: A GPX4-binding nanobody inhibited GPX4 and induced ferroptosis, so binding alone can change GPX4 function without removing the protein.
observations.context: Anti-GPX4 nanobody in cancer cell lines.

rationale.comparison: Every candidate and control is read against this construct at matched expression and matched anti-HA signal.
rationale.uncertainty: Affinity, epitope and intracellular engagement of the binder are unmeasured; the binder carries no aromatic residues, which is the composition of an idealised helical-bundle core rather than a designed hydrophobic paratope, so a flat result in every arm would first point to non-engagement. Whether binding inhibits GPX4 is unknown, and GPX4 loss causes ferroptosis, so cells need ferrostatin-1 or liproxstatin-1 during sampling.

variants.name: CHIPΔTPR fusion
variants.headline: CHIP U-box module on the binder

rationale.hypothesis: A folded catalytic U-box E3 module on the binder's C-terminus delivers E2~ubiquitin to lysines of the bound GPX4, giving K48 ubiquitination and proteasomal loss.

observations.finding: Fusing STUB1 128–303 (TPR removed) behind a designed binder through a GSGSG linker gave a ubiquibody that lowered its target in cells; the U-box point mutant R272A blocks E2 (UbcH5α) engagement.
observations.context: Binder N-terminal to CHIPΔTPR; β-galactosidase target and intrabody/monobody binders in human cells.

observations.finding: CHIP and SPOP fusions both degraded PCNA-GFP, and several binder–E3 pairs lowered H2B-GFP while others, including CRBN and DDB2 fusions, did not; activity depended on expression level (hook effect).
observations.context: Nanobody/monobody–E3 bioPROTACs against GFP-tagged nuclear targets in human cells.

observations.finding: CHIPΔTPR bioPROTACs lowered targets with half-lives of about 1.3–2.8 h in the cases measured; two binders failed, either because they blocked E2 access or because their epitope overlapped the target's lysines.
observations.context: DARPin–CHIPΔTPR fusions against GFP-type targets in cultured cells.

observations.finding: Native STUB1 ubiquitinates GPX4, with Lys191 reported as the acceptor, so GPX4 is a natural CHIP substrate.
observations.context: Imatinib-treated gastrointestinal stromal tumour cells.

observations.finding: CHIP and SPOP fusions with an N-terminal Tn3 binder failed to degrade MALT1, while VHL and TRIM21 fusions worked; avidity and orientation were implicated.
observations.context: Tn3 binder–E3 fusions against MALT1 in cultured cells; page read in part.

observations.finding: CHIP was inactive as an N-terminal E3 fusion in this format; IpaH9.8 NEL was the best of the E3s compared, and fusion autoubiquitination and self-degradation were noted.
observations.context: Recombinant bioPROTACs delivered by lipid nanoparticles; page read in part.

rationale.comparison: Against the binder-only reference for what ubiquitin ligase activity adds, and against the R272A construct to separate E2-dependent catalysis from the effect of fusing a large dimeric module.
rationale.uncertainty: CHIP fusions autoubiquitinate and may be degraded themselves; the Tn3–CHIP and nanobody–CHIP examples with the binder on the N-terminal side failed on MALT1 and in a lipid-delivered format, so the route is context-dependent. Whether the binder's epitope presents K191 or other GPX4 lysines to the U-box is unknown.

variants.note: Shared (GGGGS)2 linker replaces the GSGSG linker of the published CHIPΔTPR constructs.

features.note: Alanine in place of STUB1 R272, the E2-binding point mutation.

rationale.hypothesis: Isolates E2-dependent ubiquitin transfer from the other effects of fusing a dimeric CHIP module to the binder.

observations.finding: R272A is described as blocking the CHIP–UbcH5α interaction; the mutant ubiquibody failed to conjugate ubiquitin in vitro but gave only an intermediate target loss in cells, so it blocks some but not all E2 interactions in vivo.
observations.context: R4 ubiquibody against β-galactosidase; binder N-terminal.

rationale.comparison: Against the CHIP candidate: loss of GPX4 depletion here, with unchanged binder expression and GPX4 engagement, indicates catalysis rather than occupancy.
rationale.uncertainty: R272A leaves residual E2-dependent activity in cells, so a partial effect here would not by itself prove ubiquitin-independent loss; H260Q and P269A, which UniProt records as abolishing E3 activity, are alternative U-box-dead mutants for a later round.
rationale.edit: Removes E2 binding while keeping size, dimerisation and binder geometry.

variants.name: SPOP fusion
variants.headline: SPOP BTB/3-box module on the binder

rationale.hypothesis: A CUL3 adapter on the binder assembles a CRL3 complex next to the bound GPX4, giving cullin-dependent ubiquitination and proteasomal loss through a route independent of CHIP's E2 chemistry.

observations.finding: SPOP fusions degraded PCNA-GFP, and a SPOP fusion lowered endogenous PCNA; the control SPOP lacking the 3-box was used to test cullin dependence.
observations.context: Binder–SPOP fusions in human cells.

observations.finding: SPOP carries a MATH substrate-binding domain and a BTB/3-box region that binds CUL3 and drives dimerisation; the structure of the BTB/3-box fragment defines the helix boundaries used here.
observations.context: SPOP BTB/3-box crystal structure.

observations.finding: An N-terminal Tn3 binder fused to SPOP did not degrade MALT1, so SPOP activity depends on binder, target and orientation.
observations.context: Tn3–E3 fusions against MALT1; page read in part.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference, and against the 3-box deletion to ask whether loss of GPX4 needs CUL3 recruitment.
rationale.uncertainty: SPOP fusions dimerise, so avidity and geometry may dominate; the SPOP ortholog conservation behind these residues rests on an effective sequence number of about 3.6, so conservation says little about which positions are tolerant. Which SPOP truncation the published controls used is unconfirmed here.

variants.note: The SPOP module is residues 167–374, which includes the BTB domain, the 3-box and the C-terminal tail.

rationale.hypothesis: Isolates CUL3 recruitment from the other consequences of fusing a dimeric BTB module to the binder.

observations.finding: A SPOP control lacking the 3-box (SPOPmut) did not degrade the target the way the intact SPOP fusion did, consistent with a cullin-dependent mechanism.
observations.context: Binder–SPOP and binder–SPOPmut fusions against PCNA-GFP in human cells; exact deletion described in the supplement, not read.

rationale.comparison: Against the SPOP candidate: retention of GPX4 loss here would point to a non-CUL3 effect of the fusion.
rationale.uncertainty: The deleted span (SPOP 298–329) is my boundary from the helix records of PDB 3HTM and may not match the published control. UniProt places a homodimerisation-relevant region at 297–355, so this deletion may also weaken dimerisation, and no point mutant that cleanly abolishes CUL3 binding is known.
rationale.edit: Removes the two 3-box helices that contact CUL3 and keeps the BTB domain and C-terminal tail.

variants.name: C-terminal RRRG
variants.headline: RRRG C-end degron on the binder

rationale.hypothesis: A free C-terminal RRRG recruits a cullin-RING ligase to the binder, which ubiquitinates the bound GPX4 as well as the binder.

observations.finding: RRRG on a nanobody or leucine zipper through a 3×(GS) linker degraded cytosolic and membrane targets; a dominant-negative CUL4A/4B and MLN4924 rescued it, CUL2 perturbation did not, and MG132 rescued only slightly; replacing binder lysines with arginine improved degradation 100–204-fold.
observations.context: Degron-based bioPROTACs in engineered T-cell lines.

observations.finding: The RRRG motif comes from a cryptic degron unmasked by ligand binding, which drove rapid proteasomal degradation of fusions.
observations.context: Ligand-induced degradation system in mammalian cells.

observations.finding: C-terminal degrons ending in Arg-Gly are assigned to CRL2 adaptors, which conflicts with the CUL4 rescue seen with RRRG in the T-cell work.
observations.context: Proteome-wide screen of C-terminal degrons.

rationale.comparison: Against the TRGN construct to isolate the degron, and against the reference for the binder-alone baseline.
rationale.uncertainty: Which cullin reads RRRG is unresolved (CUL4 in one study, CRL2 in the degron surveys), so cullin rescue must be read carefully. The binder carries eight lysines that compete with GPX4 for ubiquitin and the degron will mark the degrader itself for destruction, possibly before GPX4 is modified; the shared (GGGGS)2 linker differs from the 3×(GS) linker of the precedent.

rationale.hypothesis: Isolates the RRRG degron from the effect of adding any four residues to the C-terminus of the binder.

observations.finding: TRGN was the no-degron control for RRRG and did not degrade the targets.
observations.context: Same T-cell bioPROTAC system.

rationale.comparison: Against the RRRG construct at matched expression; a difference in GPX4 depletion attributes the effect to the degron.
rationale.uncertainty: TRGN does not exclude differences in binder stability or expression, so anti-HA level must be matched.
rationale.edit: Same length and free C-terminus as RRRG, without the degron's terminal Arg-Gly pairing.

variants.name: C-terminal CMA motif
variants.headline: KFERQ-type CMA motif on the binder

rationale.hypothesis: A KFERQ-type targeting motif lets HSC70 carry the binder-bound GPX4 to the lysosome, removing GPX4 without ubiquitination and without the degrader's own lysines acting as competing acceptors.

observations.finding: The 14-residue targeting motif, placed C-terminal to a target-binding domain, drove lysosomal degradation of bound endogenous proteins; degradation was blocked by NH4Cl or pepstatin and was not affected by 3-methyladenine or MG132.
observations.context: CTM fusions in cultured cells; full text read.

observations.finding: GPX4 is degraded by chaperone-mediated autophagy through HSC70 and LAMP2A during ferroptosis.
observations.context: Cancer cells treated with ferroptosis inducers.

observations.finding: Hydroxylation of GPX4 at Pro186 by EGLN3 blocks its chaperone-mediated autophagic degradation.
observations.context: Cancer cell lines.

observations.finding: KFERQ-type tags can also deliver targets through endosomal microautophagy, which needs VPS4A and not LAMP2A.
observations.context: Targeting-chimera fusions in cultured cells.

rationale.comparison: Against the mutated-motif construct to isolate motif-dependent targeting, and against the reference for binder-alone effects.
rationale.uncertainty: CMA needs the substrate to unfold; a stable helical binder in a tight complex with GPX4 may resist this, and GPX4 hydroxylation at Pro186 or competition by p23 for HSC70 may block the native route. The motif may act through endosomal microautophagy rather than LAMP2A-CMA, so rescue patterns must separate the two.

rationale.hypothesis: Isolates motif-dependent HSC70 recruitment from the effect of adding a 14-residue basic, charged tail to the binder.

observations.finding: The patent states, in its Figure 1 legend and description, that changing the two glutamines of the targeting motif to alanine inactivates it, without giving the residue positions in the text read.
observations.context: CMA-targeting fusion proteins; claims not read.

rationale.comparison: Against the CTM candidate; the same GPX4 loss here would indicate a motif-independent effect.
rationale.uncertainty: The two substituted positions (Q5 and Q10 of the motif) are my rule-based choice, since the published positions are not given in the text read, so this control is exploratory and its inactivity is not demonstrated.
rationale.edit: Replaces the glutamine of KFERQ and of QRFFE with alanine.

precedent_search.scope: Europe PMC, PubMed, publisher pages and patents, to 2025-12-31: binder-E3 fusions (bioPROTACs, ubiquibodies, AdPROM), C-end degrons, CMA targeting motifs, small-molecule and protein GPX4 degraders, and native GPX4 turnover routes. No protein-binder–E3 or binder–degron fusion against GPX4 was found before 2026; later reports were excluded by the evidence cutoff and not used.

attempted_analyses.reason: UniRef50 cluster of Q9UNE7 held 19 UniProtKB sequences, below the floor of 30, and the only Pfam fallback (PF12895, ANAPC3/TPR) describes the TPR repeats that the retained 128–303 region lacks.
attempted_analyses.attempted: UniProt REST fetch for Q9UNE7 at the ortholog level, refused by the fetcher.

attempted_analyses.reason: De novo designed sequence with no database accession and no natural homologs, so there is no ortholog set to align.
attempted_analyses.attempted: No fetch possible; the sequence has no UniProt entry.

sites.label: R272 — E2-binding residue of the U-box

observations.finding: R272A blocks CHIP's interaction with UbcH5α; the mutant ubiquibody failed to conjugate ubiquitin in vitro and gave only partial target loss in cells.
observations.context: R4 ubiquibody against β-galactosidase.

sites.note: Construct position 227 corresponds to STUB1 residue 272.

observations.finding: The same substitution in a CHIPΔTPR ubiquibody blocks E2 engagement and ubiquitin conjugation in vitro, with an intermediate effect in cells.
observations.context: R4 ubiquibody against β-galactosidase.

sites.label: Q5 and Q10 — glutamines of the KFERQ-type motifs

observations.finding: Changing the two glutamines of the targeting motif to alanine inactivates it, according to the patent description.
observations.context: CMA-targeting fusion proteins; positions not stated in the text read.

sites.note: The patent text read does not give the positions; the assignment of these two glutamines is mine.

sites.label: Q5A and Q10A — glutamines replaced
sites.note: Exploratory rule-based inactive control; inactivity has not been shown for these positions.

sites.label: C-terminal Arg–Gly of the degron

observations.finding: C-terminal degrons ending in Arg-Gly are recognised by cullin-RING adaptors and need a free carboxylate.
observations.context: Proteome-wide C-terminal degron screen.

sites.note: The terminal Gly must remain the last residue of the chain.

method.comparison_set: UniProtKB members of UniRef50_O43791, the UniRef50 cluster containing O43791: the same protein in other species, clustered by UniProt at 50% identity with an 80% length-overlap requirement. ORTHOLOG level: scores answer what this protein needs.
method.alignment: multiple alignment by FAMSA via pyfamsa 0.7.0, projected onto reference coordinates by dropping columns where the reference is gapped. It can score positions that MAFFT leaves unscored, with weak support, so read per-position coverage alongside the score
method.weighting: Henikoff position-based sequence weights, computed over variable columns only
method.effective_sequences_definition: Neff = sum(1/n_i), n_i counting sequences at least 80% identical to sequence i over positions where both have a residue (itself included); pairs overlapping less than 50% of the reference are not counted as similar. Reported unnormalised and divided by reference length; normalisation is not standardised in the literature, so compare only against values computed the same way. This is NOT the sum of the Henikoff weights, which is rescaled to the sequence count by construction and therefore always equals it.
method.score: Jensen-Shannon divergence against Robinson & Robinson background, scaled by column occupancy (Capra & Singh 2007)

method.score: Jensen-Shannon divergence against Robinson & Robinson background, scaled by column occupancy (Capra & Singh 2007)
method.mapping: Scores from the donor-level SPOP result are placed at the construct positions occupied by SPOP residues; every other position is unscored.
